problem: The critical point of the function $f(x)=(2x+1){e}^{x-2}$ is $x=${{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡3x+\operatorname{cos}⁡3x.$ If the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})$ are $x={x}_{1}$ and $x={x}_{2},$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
A critical point of $f(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $f$ such that either ${f}^{′}(c)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(c)$ does not exist.

Differentiating $f(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡3x+\operatorname{cos}⁡3x) \\  & =3(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3x)+(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3x) \\  & =9\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the critical points:

- First, we compute the points where ${f}^{′}(c)=0.$ We set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3x & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡3x & =9\operatorname{cos}⁡3x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡3x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡3x} & =\frac{9}{3}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡3x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡3x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡3x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡3+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡3+\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\frac{\pi }{3}<x<\frac{\pi }{3}.$

- setting $n=-1$ gives $x≈-0.630\,85$ to five decimal places

- setting $n=0$ gives $x≈0.416\,35$ to five decimal places

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\frac{\pi }{3}<x<\frac{\pi }{3}.$ So, the solutions to this equation for $x\in (-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})$ are 

$$
x≈-0.630\,85,\,x≈0.416\,35.
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ has stationary points at $x≈-0.630\,85$ and $x≈0.416\,35.$

- Second, we note that ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists for all values of $x\in (-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}).$ So $f(x)$ has no non-stationary critical points.

Therefore, we conclude that the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})$ are ${x}_{1}≈-0.630\,85$ and ${x}_{2}≈0.416\,35.$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}≈-0.630\,85\cdot 0.416\,35≈-0.26
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
